title: Bounded cotangent dimension makes an Artinian inverse limit Noetherian and adic
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring and $l$ a field finite as a $\Lambda$-module [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-field]. Let $\cdots\twoheadrightarrow A_{n+1}\xrightarrow{q_n} A_n\twoheadrightarrow\cdots\twoheadrightarrow A_1$ be a sequence, indexed by integers $n\geq1$, of surjective morphisms in $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,l}$ [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Suppose there is an integer $d\geq0$ such that $\dim_l(\mathfrak m_{A_n}/\mathfrak m_{A_n}^2)\leq d$ for every $n$, where the vector-space structures use the specified residue field $l$. Define the ring $B=\{(a_n)\in\prod_{n\geq1}A_n:q_n(a_{n+1})=a_n\text{ for every }n\}$ with componentwise operations and the diagonal $\Lambda$-structure. Then $B$ is a Noetherian local $\Lambda$-algebra with specified residue field $l$ and is complete for its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Each coordinate map $p_n:B\to A_n$ is a surjective local residue-preserving $\Lambda$-map. With $I_n=\ker p_n$, the kernel filtration and the powers of $\mathfrak m_B$ are cofinal: for every $r\geq1$ there exists $n\geq1$ with $I_n\subseteq\mathfrak m_B^r$, and for every $n\geq1$ there exists $r\geq1$ with $\mathfrak m_B^r\subseteq I_n$.

source.place: Tag 06SF (lemma-limit-artinian), including surjectivity of projections used in its proof

proof.text: The coordinate maps are surjective: to lift $a\in A_n$, choose successively a preimage in $A_{n+1}$, then in $A_{n+2}$, and so on; the earlier coordinates are forced by the transition maps. All coordinates of a compatible sequence have the same residue in $l$. This gives a surjection $\rho:B\to l$, and set $\mathfrak m_B=\ker\rho$. If $b\notin\mathfrak m_B$, each $b_n$ is a unit of the local ring $A_n$; the sequence $(b_n^{-1})_n$ is compatible and is an inverse in $B$. If $b\in\mathfrak m_B$, it cannot be a unit because its residue is zero. Thus $B$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ and specified residue field $l$. Each $p_n$ preserves the residue marking, and $p_n^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{A_n})=\mathfrak m_B$, so it is local.

source.place: Tag 06SF (lemma-limit-artinian), opening sentence of proof; componentwise inverse and recursive lifting made explicit

proof.text: Surjectivity and the residue markings imply that $q_n$ maps $\mathfrak m_{A_{n+1}}$ onto $\mathfrak m_{A_n}$, hence gives a surjection on their quotients by squares. Therefore their dimensions are nondecreasing integers bounded by $d$; choose $N$ after they stabilize, with value $r$. Choose a basis of $\mathfrak m_{A_N}/\mathfrak m_{A_N}^2$, representatives in $\mathfrak m_{A_N}$, and lift them by $p_N$ to $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in\mathfrak m_B$. For $n\geq N$ the cotangent map to level $N$ is a surjection between $r$-dimensional spaces and hence an isomorphism, so the images of these $x_i$ form a basis. For $n<N$ their classes still span, by surjectivity from level $N$. Each $A_n$ is Noetherian by the Artinian-local lemma, so its maximal ideal is finitely generated. Apply the cited local-generator form of Nakayama with $M=\mathfrak m_{A_n}$: the images of the $x_i$ generate that ideal for every $n$. Also choose $c_n\geq1$ with $\mathfrak m_{A_n}^{c_n}=0$ by the same Artinian-local lemma.

source.place: Tag 06SF (lemma-limit-artinian), stabilization and common generators; algebra.tex Tags 00KH, 00J8 and 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (8)

proof.text: Choose finitely many $\Lambda$-module generators of $l$; they also generate $l$ as a $\Lambda$-algebra. Lift them through $\rho$ to $y_1,\ldots,y_t\in B$. Evaluation defines $f:P=\Lambda[Y_1,\ldots,Y_t,X_1,\ldots,X_r]\to B$ with $Y_j\mapsto y_j$, $X_i\mapsto x_i$. Its residue map $e:P\to l$ is surjective and sends $X_i$ to zero. For each $n$, the composite $f_n:P\to A_n$ is surjective as follows. Write $x_i$ also for their images in $A_n$. For any $a\in A_n$ choose a polynomial in the $y_j$ with the same residue, so the error lies in $\mathfrak m_{A_n}$. If an error lies in $\mathfrak m_{A_n}^h$, write it as a finite sum $\sum_{|\alpha|=h}a_\alpha x^\alpha$, since the $x_i$ generate the maximal ideal. Replace each $a_\alpha$ by a polynomial in the $y_j$ with the same residue; subtracting the resulting polynomial changes the error to one in $\mathfrak m_{A_n}^{h+1}$. Iterating for $h=1,\ldots,c_n-1$ kills the error. This proves surjectivity without assuming a coefficient field in any $A_n$.

source.place: Tag 06SF (lemma-limit-artinian), polynomial presentation; nilpotent approximation giving its surjectivity written out

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak q=\ker(e)$ and $R=\varprojlim_hP/\mathfrak q^h$. Apply the completed-polynomial test-ring lemma with base $\Lambda$, field $l$, $s=t$ and $d=r$ (finite as a module implies finite type as used in the preceding step). It says that $R$ is Noetherian complete local with residue field $l$ and that each residue-compatible $f_n$ extends uniquely to a local $\Lambda$-map $g_n:R\to A_n$. The maps $g_n$ are surjective because their images contain $f_n(P)=A_n$. Their uniqueness gives $q_n g_{n+1}=g_n$, since both maps restrict to $f_n$ on $P$. Set $J_n=\ker(g_n)$ and $J=\bigcap_nJ_n$. These are decreasing proper ideals, $J_n\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$, and $\mathfrak m_R^{c_n}\subseteq J_n$: a product of $c_n$ elements of $\mathfrak m_R$ maps into $\mathfrak m_{A_n}^{c_n}=0$.

source.place: Tag 06SF (lemma-limit-artinian), completion R and its compatible surjective maps; completed-polynomial construction from Tag 06SM (lemma-exists-smooth)

proof.text: Let $T=R/J$ and $\mathfrak m_T=\mathfrak m_R/J$. Because $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$, $T$ is local with this maximal ideal and residue field $l$: an element outside $\mathfrak m_T$ lifts to a unit in $R$. It is Noetherian: the inverse image of any ideal of $T$ is a finitely generated ideal of $R$, and the images of these generators generate the given ideal. The $R$-module $T$ is cyclic, generated by $1$. Thus the finite-module completeness lemma applied to the Noetherian ring $R$, its ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, and the finite module $T$, makes the canonical map $T\to\varprojlim_hT/\mathfrak m_R^hT$ bijective. Here $\mathfrak m_R^hT=\mathfrak m_T^h$ as ideals of $T$, so $T$ is complete for its maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 06SF (lemma-limit-artinian), quotient R/J; algebra.tex Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (3), and Tag 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local)

proof.text: To apply the descending-ideal lemma with its exact indexing hypothesis, choose strictly increasing positive integers $e_n\geq c_n$, tending to infinity. For positive $h<e_1$ set $K_h=\mathfrak m_R$; for $e_n\leq h<e_{n+1}$ set $K_h=J_n$. Then $K_h$ is decreasing, $\mathfrak m_R^h\subseteq K_h$, and $\bigcap_hK_h=J$. The descending-ideal lemma applied to $R$ and $(K_h)$ gives, for every $a\geq1$, some $h$ with $K_h\subseteq J+\mathfrak m_R^a$. There is an original $J_n\subseteq K_h$ (take $n=1$ in the initial block and the block index otherwise). Hence some $J_n\subseteq J+\mathfrak m_R^a$. Conversely, each $J_n$ contains $\mathfrak m_R^{c_n}$. Passing to $T$ proves that $L_n=J_n/J$ and $\mathfrak m_T^a$ are cofinal. This handles arbitrary nilpotence exponents rather than presuming $c_n=n$.

The maps $g_n$ give $\phi:T\to B$ and identifications $T/L_n\cong A_n$, all with the specified quotient maps. Here is the explicit inverse-limit comparison using the cofinality just proved. Choose increasing indices $n(a)\geq a$ with $L_{n(a)}\subseteq\mathfrak m_T^a$. For $b=(b_n)\in B$, regard $b_{n(a)}$ as an element of $T/L_{n(a)}$ and map it to $T/\mathfrak m_T^a$. These residues are compatible, so completeness of $T$ gives a unique $t\in T$. For a fixed $n$ choose $a\geq c_n$ with $n(a)\geq n$; since $\mathfrak m_T^a\subseteq L_n$, the residue of $t$ in $T/L_n$ is exactly $b_n$. Thus $\phi(t)=b$. Also $\ker\phi=\bigcap_n L_n=0$, because $J=\bigcap_nJ_n$. Therefore $\phi$ is a bijective $\Lambda$-ring map, with $p_n\phi$ precisely the map induced by $g_n$.

source.place: Tag 06SF (lemma-limit-artinian), identification R/J = lim R/J_n = lim A_n, via explicit maps

proof.text: The isomorphism $\phi$ preserves the common residue map to $l$, so it sends $\mathfrak m_T$ to $\mathfrak m_B$, their powers to the corresponding powers, and $L_n=\ker(T\to A_n)$ to $I_n=\ker(p_n)$. The Noetherianity and maximal-ideal completeness of $T$ therefore give those properties for $B$. The two containments of step 6 become, respectively, $I_n\subseteq\mathfrak m_B^a$ for a suitable $n$ for every $a$, and $\mathfrak m_B^{c_n}\subseteq I_n$ for every $n$. Along with step 1 these are every claimed conclusion.

(2) q_n maps m onto m, so the cotangent dimensions are nondecreasing and at most d and they stabilize. The lifted basis spans at every level. Nakayama applies to the finitely generated m_{A_n}; the Artinian node supplies Noetherianity and c_n. (3) Approximation with m^h = (x^α : |α| = h) holds with no coefficient field. (4) The completed-polynomial lemma's hypotheses hold (Λ Noetherian, l finite type, e onto with e(X_i) = 0, and f_n composed with the residue map is e). Uniqueness gives q_n g_{n+1} = g_n, and m_R^{c_n} ⊆ J_n. (5) The finite-module completeness lemma for the cyclic module T = R/J over the m_R-complete R holds because m_R^h T = m_T^h. (6) The block renumbering K_h satisfies the exact hypothesis m^h ⊆ K_h of the descending-ideal lemma: K_h is decreasing and ∩K_h = J. This closes the renumbering gap that Stacks notes. (7–8) The comparison φ: T → B is explicit: compatible residues give a t, the kernel is ∩L_n = 0, and residues, powers and kernels are transported. proof_deps equals the union of step uses. No cycle. The only cited node from another unit, lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian, is a generic algebra tool; I accept the declared tool_use. No SGA. Edge cases checked: k[t]/(t^n), constant tower, d = 0, Z/p^n, stretched c_n; the unbounded-dimension counterexample shows the bound is needed. No changes.
